finding.title: Inject RewardMilestoneService into CompletionRepositoryImpl instead of constructing it ad hoc per call
finding.why: Both markComplete and _markCompleteSingleInTransaction build a fresh RewardMilestoneService with `new` instead of receiving it via the constructor, unlike CompletionDetectionService which completionRepositoryProvider correctly injects. There is no seam to substitute a fake reward-milestone evaluator in a repository-level test without exercising the real Drift-backed class (Feathers), and any future dependency added to RewardMilestoneService must be threaded through by hand at both call sites.
finding.recommendation: Accept RewardMilestoneService as an optional constructor parameter on CompletionRepositoryImpl (defaulting to a provider-supplied instance), matching the existing pattern for CompletionDetectionService/BookmarkRepository in the same class.
acceptance_criteria: RewardMilestoneService is injected via CompletionRepositoryImpl's constructor; no `RewardMilestoneService(...)` construction remains inside markComplete or _markCompleteSingleInTransaction.

finding.title: Wire BatchPlan into CompletionWriter.commitBatch or delete the unused sealed hierarchy and its test

evidence.quote: /// [CompletionWriter.commitBatch] receives a [BatchPlan] so it knows which

finding.why: batch_plan.dart's own doc comment asserts CompletionWriter.commitBatch takes a BatchPlan; the real signature takes a raw List<CompletionCommand> and never references BatchPlan anywhere in lib/ — grep confirms the only non-doc-comment usages of BatchPlan/LiveBatchPlan/BulkInTrackPlan/LifetimeOnlyPlan are inside batch_plan_test.dart itself (132 lines exercising a class nothing production calls). The same three-tier classification BatchPlan.classify already encodes is instead re-derived independently via CompletionRepositoryImpl._bulkSourceFor — an Evans-lens 'invariant re-derived instead of enforced once' split that could silently diverge (e.g. a fourth CompletionSource value added later would need updating in two unconnected places). MarkCompletionResult.newMilestoneUnlocks is a related vestige of the same pre-DEC-32 design — it is now hard-coded to `const []` at every call site since the auto-unlock ladder was replaced by the spend economy.
finding.recommendation: Either make CompletionWriter.commitBatch accept a BatchPlan and delete _bulkSourceFor in favor of BatchPlan.classify, or delete batch_plan.dart and batch_plan_test.dart as speculative generality that was superseded before it shipped.
acceptance_criteria: grep for `BatchPlan` in lib/ returns either a real call site inside completion_writer.dart/completion_repository_impl.dart, or zero results (type and test deleted); the doc comment on the class matches what actually calls it.

finding.title: Narrow and log the catch-all in CompletionRepositoryImpl._appendStreakEvent

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // Defensive: never let a telemetry tee block the primary write.

finding.why: catch (_) swallows every exception from BOTH the streak_events Drift insert and the outbox enqueue (facade.enqueueStreakPayload) with no AppLogger call anywhere in this file — a codec bug, closed-DB race, or genuine corruption is indistinguishable from the expected benign duplicate-key case this comment is defending against. This is also EH-4-adjacent (catches Error subtypes, not just typed Exceptions) and evades the Rule-0 'no empty catch blocks' Makefile grep (`catch\s*(_\?\w*)\s*{}`), which only matches a literal same-line `{}` — this multi-line comment-only body is functionally empty but textually invisible to that checker. Per the file's own header comment, the outbox enqueue here is what 'closes the gap' where a second device sees a frozen streak; if enqueueStreakPayload throws, that gap silently reopens with zero diagnostic trail and no retry.
finding.recommendation: Catch a specific expected type (e.g. the Drift unique-constraint exception) for the benign-duplicate case and let everything else propagate or be logged via AppLogger.instance.warning/error before swallowing, so a genuine failure is at least visible in Crashlytics/Talker.
acceptance_criteria: The catch narrows to the specific expected exception type; every other path logs via AppLogger before returning; a regression test that makes enqueueStreakPayload throw asserts the failure is logged, not silently dropped.

finding.title: Add the required inline keepAlive justification to CompletionCommitted and OptimisticCompletionState
finding.why: Both classes have doc comments explaining what they do, but neither explains why keepAlive: true (vs default autoDispose) is required. The codebase already has an established convention for this — content_providers.dart:12, sync_orchestrator_providers.dart:51 and pin_flow_controller.dart:127 all lead with 'keepAlive: ...' explicitly justifying the lifecycle choice — so this is a real, checkable deviation from a convention this same codebase demonstrably follows elsewhere, not a style nit invented for this review.
finding.recommendation: Prefix each doc comment (or add an adjacent `// keepAlive: ...` line) explicitly stating why autoDispose would break the provider — e.g. 'keepAlive: true — must survive across screens so completion-dependent providers can detect a commit that happened while they were unmounted.'
acceptance_criteria: Both keepAlive: true annotations carry an adjacent comment starting with 'keepAlive:' explaining the lifecycle choice, matching the convention in content_providers.dart / sync_orchestrator_providers.dart.

finding.title: Remove the completion_source.dart re-export from mark_completion_use_case.dart
finding.why: coding-standards.md Rule 2 states providers.dart is 'the only sanctioned re-export file... do not add other barrel/re-export files — deep re-export chains defeat "where is X defined?" search'. mark_completion_use_case.dart re-exports a domain entity from an unrelated file. This isn't theoretical: mark_completion_use_case_siyum_routing_test.dart imports only the use-case file and uses CompletionSource entirely via the transitive re-export, demonstrating exactly the defined-where? confusion the rule warns about.
finding.recommendation: Delete the export statement; update the one demonstrated consumer (and any others `dart analyze` surfaces) to import completion_source.dart directly.
acceptance_criteria: mark_completion_use_case.dart has no export statement; all consumers of CompletionSource import completion_source.dart directly; `dart analyze` stays clean.
